issues.claim: `StringBuilderPooledObjectPolicy` clears the `StringBuilder` in its `Return` method and refuses to keep instances whose capacity has exceeded a configured limit.
issues.problem: The behaviour matches the Microsoft.Extensions.ObjectPool source as I recall it, with Clear() and MaximumRetainedCapacity. The fetched ObjectPool excerpt is truncated and only shows that a policy defines how an object is reset on return. It does not show the Clear call or the capacity limit.
issues.suggestedFix: Cite the StringBuilderPooledObjectPolicy API page (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.extensions.objectpool.stringbuilderpooledobjectpolicy) or the dotnet/aspnetcore source. Otherwise soften the sentence to say the policy resets the builder on return.

issues.claim: For `StringBuilder` that is `Clear()`: it removes all characters (the same as `Length = 0`) but keeps the already allocated buffer.
issues.problem: The Clear page excerpt supports only "equivalent to setting Length to 0". It does not say the allocated buffer or capacity is retained. I believe this is true for the common case, but it is not shown.
issues.suggestedFix: Soften it to say Clear removes the characters and does not discard the builder's capacity, and cite the Capacity or Length documentation. Alternatively drop the buffer-retention clause.
